sources.title: qwen-max Model Info
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The qwen-max card still explicitly maps the rolling alias to qwen-max-2025-01-25 and describes only a parameter scale of hundreds of billions. It gives no nominal total or activated parameter count. Text modalities, 32768 context and regional function-calling differences remain on the card.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Max: Exploring the Intelligence of Large-scale MoE Model
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The January 28, 2025 announcement identifies Qwen2.5-Max as a large-scale MoE pretrained on over 20 trillion tokens, then post-trained with SFT and RLHF, and binds it to API ID qwen-max-2025-01-25. It publishes neither total nor active size. Qwen2.5-72B is a comparison model, not an identified base for Max; 20 trillion measures training tokens, not parameters.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio model pricing
sources.evidence: Exact qwen-max rows specify non-thinking mode only, including International deployment.

sources.title: Text generation models
sources.evidence: Legacy Qwen table groups qwen-max and snapshots at 128k context, with thinking unsupported and function calling supported. This conflicts with the exact model card context and omits regional tool limitations.

sources.title: Model lifecycle and updates
sources.evidence: Beijing release table lists qwen-max on 2024-10-15 and describes rolling updates; it does not establish the baseline 2024-04-03 as initial alias release.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Launches First Cloud Region in Brazil to Accelerate Cloud and AI Transformation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Alibaba identifies Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B as the first open release of a Qwen-Max-class model and publishes 2.4 trillion total and 95 billion active parameters for that named release. It does not bind those sizes or weights to the older qwen-max-2025-01-25 snapshot. Also identifies Qwen as developed by Alibaba.

sources.title: Models.dev qwen-max record
sources.evidence: Baseline source gives release_date 2024-04-03 and last_updated 2025-01-25, without primary evidence for the initial date.

sources.title: qwen-max Model Info (international documentation)
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The international card, last updated October 11, still maps qwen-max to qwen-max-2025-01-25. Its only size description is hundreds of billions; no nominal total or active figure is supplied. It specifies 32768 context and 30720 maximum input in a shared table, with separate Beijing and Singapore capability rows.

sources.title: qwen-max model information (Chinese documentation)
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The Chinese exact-model card describes a Qwen2.5 model at the hundred-billion scale (千亿级别), explicitly maps it to qwen-max-2025-01-25, and provides no nominal total or active count. Its shared context table remains 32768 with no 128k Beijing alternative.

sources.title: Qwen Series Model Free Quota Validity Period Adjustment Notice
sources.evidence: Quota change effective September 19, 2024 lists qwen-max separately from qwen-max-0403, qwen-max-0428 and qwen-max-0107. Establishes availability by that date, not the original release date, and shows why a snapshot suffix must not establish alias introduction.

sources.title: Qwen2.5 Technical Report, revision 2
sources.evidence: The January 3, 2025 report cited by the Qwen2.5-Max launch post names open dense models from 0.5B through 72B and proprietary MoE models Qwen2.5-Turbo and Qwen2.5-Plus. Sections 1-2 and the architecture table do not identify Qwen2.5-Max as a variant of any sized model. The family-level dense-to-MoE construction description is not a named-base lineage for Max and cannot supply its total or active size.

sources.title: Qwen3: Think Deeper, Act Faster
sources.evidence: April 29, 2025 release explicitly assigns 235B total and 22B activated parameters to Qwen3-235B-A22B, and 30B total and 3B activated to Qwen3-30B-A3B. These are separately named later models; the announcement does not identify either as the base or equivalent checkpoint of Qwen2.5-Max. Their nominal sizes therefore cannot populate this historical record.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Max: Exploring large-scale MoE intelligence (Chinese announcement)
sources.evidence: The Chinese January 28, 2025 announcement independently describes Qwen2.5-Max as a large-scale MoE, more than 20 trillion pretraining tokens and subsequent post-training. It compares Max with Qwen2.5-72B and gives no numerical total or activated parameter count or named sized base model.

name.note: Display spelling of the official Qwen-Max name.

family.note: Qwen; this alias currently maps to Qwen2.5-Max.

release_date.note: Initial alias release date remains unverified: baseline 2024-04-03 has no located primary announcement. The September 19, 2024 quota notice already lists qwen-max separately from qwen-max-0403, so the October 15, 2024 lifecycle entry cannot establish its original availability. January 28, 2025 is the announcement of the later Qwen2.5-Max snapshot. Patch clears the unsupported date rather than substituting one of these different events.

open_weights.note: Exact older model is served through API/Qwen Chat; the later Qwen3.8 release is explicitly the first open Max-class release. Do not transfer its weights to qwen-max.

license.note: No open-weight license applies to this hosted model; service terms are distinct. Do not inherit licenses from open Qwen checkpoints.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search and reopened primary sources establish only hundred-billion-scale size for qwen-max, still mapped to qwen-max-2025-01-25 (Qwen2.5-Max). This is not a nominal point count. No developer-published nominal total or explicit lineage to a named model with a known size was located. The launch compares against Qwen2.5-72B rather than identifying it as the base; its cited technical report covers other named dense and MoE models. Qwen3 and Qwen3.8 disclosures apply to distinct later releases. Null reflects absence of a supported nominal count, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: No nominal activated-per-token count, expert configuration sufficient to establish one, or explicit named-base relationship with a known active size was located for Qwen2.5-Max. The official MoE designation is insufficient to infer the active count. The 22B figure belongs to Qwen3-235B-A22B and 95B to Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, neither bound to the January 2025 snapshot.

architecture.note: Applies to the currently documented qwen-max-2025-01-25 mapping, explicitly named Qwen2.5-Max in the developer announcement. Not a claim about every historical alias revision.

context_window.note: Exact alias cards, including international documentation updated October 11, 2026, map to qwen-max-2025-01-25 and state 32768. The October 15, 2026 overview states 128k for qwen-max and snapshots. Neither exact card specifies a Beijing/Singapore context difference, and no primary upgrade notice resolving the discrepancy was located. 32768 remains the strongest exact-snapshot evidence, but the current canonical alias limit is unresolved; clear the unqualified numeric field pending resolution.

modalities.note: Both listed regions specify text input and text output.

reasoning.note: No dedicated thinking mode; ordinary reasoning capabilities do not imply a reasoning-output mode.

tool_call.note: Supported in Beijing; the exact card marks Singapore unsupported. Boolean means support exists, not uniform availability across regions.

description.value: Hosted Qwen text model for multilingual chat and coding, currently mapped to the Qwen2.5-Max snapshot.
description.note: Replaces generic flagship and agentic marketing with the exact hosted identity; later flagship generations are separate models.

patch.description: Hosted Qwen text model for multilingual chat and coding, currently mapped to the Qwen2.5-Max snapshot.
patch.notes: Rolling hosted alias: MoE architecture refers to the documented qwen-max-2025-01-25 (Qwen2.5-Max) mapping. Alibaba describes a hundred-billion-scale model but publishes no nominal total or active parameter count for this snapshot; later Qwen3/Qwen3.8 sizes do not apply. Current context is unresolved: exact model cards state 32768, including the October 11, 2026 international card; the October 15 overview says 128k. No region-specific context difference or upgrade announcement was verified. Function calling is supported in Beijing but marked unsupported in Singapore. Initial alias release date is unverified; the alias was listed by September 19, 2024, separately from the 0403 snapshot. January 28, 2025 announces the later Qwen2.5-Max snapshot.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit confirms the qwen-max alias still maps to Qwen2.5-Max (qwen-max-2025-01-25). Reopened English/Chinese cards and launch posts, checked the cited technical report, and searched newer developer disclosures and named-base lineage. No nominal total or active count is supported: hundred-billion-scale wording is broad, 20 trillion counts training tokens, Qwen2.5-72B is a benchmark comparator, and later Qwen3/Qwen3.8 counts belong to other models. Explicitly retains null for both counts and parameters_source, with verified MoE architecture unchanged. Other audited fields and their existing release-date/context uncertainties are preserved.
